gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay at home tonight, if that is all right.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference: would rather stay.

gaps.sentence: That ___ be Sarah at the door — she is in Berlin until Friday.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' expresses logical impossibility: can't be Sarah.

gaps.sentence: ___ I use your phone for a local call?
Students ___ to hand in essays by Friday at the latest.
gaps.hint: ought to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' takes the full infinitive, so only 'ought' fits before 'to': ought.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have hurried — the concert was cancelled anyway.
gaps.hint: the rush turned out to be unnecessary
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have hurried' means we hurried although it was unnecessary: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: ___ I get you something from the shop while I am out?
gaps.hint: making an offer with shall I
gaps.explanation: 'Shall I' offers to do something: Shall.

gaps.sentence: The medicine ___ be kept out of the reach of children.
gaps.explanation: Written instructions use 'must' for essential requirements: must be kept.
